the sixth transmemebrane domain of Pgp1 plays a critical role in the specificity of drug accumulation in multidrugsistant cells and that the sensitivity of this domain to reversal agents is a function of the specific amino acid residues present in the domain.

the sixth trans-membrane domain of Pgp1 plays a critical role in determining both drug accumulation levels in the presence or absence of a drug efflux inhibitor as well as in conferring a unique multidrug resistance phenotype that is sensitive or insensitive to drug efflux inhibition by cyclosporins.

the expression of a Pgp1 cDNA encoding two substitutions in the sixth TM domain confers a unique multidrug resistance phenotype that displays preferential cross-resistance to actinomycins and decreased cross-resistance to colchicines and anthracyclines.

the identification of mutations that alter the structure and function of Pgp1 and the use of such mutants to identify regions of Pgp1 that are important for drug transport.
the molecular mechanism of Pgp1 and the molecular mechanism of multidrug resistance.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the multidrug transporter Pgp1.

mutations in the sixth trans-membrane domain of Pgp1 can alter the sensitivity of the protein to reversal agents and can alter the pattern of drug resistance.

the sixth trans-membrane domain of Pgp1 plays a critical role in determining the drug specificity and sensitivity of the transporter.
